gaps.sentence: The medicine had an immediate ___ on her breathing.
gaps.explanation: 'An effect on' — the noun form is required here.

gaps.sentence: Take my ___ and sell the car before the prices fall.
gaps.explanation: 'Take my advice' — the noun form follows the possessive.

gaps.sentence: Should any dispute ___, the matter will go to arbitration.
gaps.explanation: 'Arise' = (problems, disputes) occur; 'rise' means go up and 'raise' needs an object.

gaps.sentence: Could I ___ your pen for a moment?
gaps.hint: meaning: take and return later (from someone's point of view)
gaps.explanation: 'Borrow' means to take something temporarily; 'lend' means to give something temporarily to someone else.

gaps.sentence: Unemployment has ___ sharply since the spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Has risen' — rise does not take an object.

gaps.sentence: One of the screws on the bracket has come ___.

gaps.explanation: 'Lately' means recently and is typical with the present perfect; 'late' means behind time.

gaps.sentence: I start my new ___ at the hospital on Monday.
gaps.hint: a single, countable position of employment
gaps.explanation: 'Job' is countable — one particular position; 'work' is uncountable and cannot follow 'a new'.
